role.altitude: The landscape architect keeps meeting clients and partners, walking sites, interpreting conditions, drawing designs and deciding what to keep; hunting the latest drawings in mail, loading site data layer by layer, taking off quantities and copying specification clauses shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working in a common data environment
role.ambitious_version: A designer whose quantities, clauses and site layers follow from the model, leaving time for the design.

tasks.short: Arrange meetings, collect the latest drawings and open issues, confer with clients, engineering personnel or architects on landscape projects, record agreements and issues, and send the notes.

steps.what: Landscape architect arranges meetings with clients and partners
Partners upload their latest drawings to the common data environment: by mail today
Landscape architect collects the latest drawings and open issues for the meeting
Landscape architect confers with clients, engineering personnel or architects on the landscape project
Landscape architect writes up agreements and issues in the minutes and the issue list
Landscape architect checks the final minutes and issue list: agreements, owners and dates as agreed in the meeting
Landscape architect sends the checked notes to the client and partners

tasks.design: A scheduling poll finds meeting times. Partners upload drawings to a common data environment, so the latest versions and open issues are in one place instead of in mail threads. Issues raised in the meeting are logged once, against the drawing, instead of typed into minutes and then copied to a separate issue list. Conferring and sending the notes stay with the architect.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes and issue list exactly as checked by the architect in s5, sent once to the client and partners who attended; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings and issue lists moved by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Common data environments with drawing-based issue tracking.
tasks.still_hard: Clients who do not use the shared environment.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the client and the engineer to agree on a level change.
tasks.altitude: Less hunting and copying; conferring stays.

evidence.claim: Drawings and issue lists by mail glue teams today; a common data environment with model-based issue tracking replaces them.

assumptions: Boundary: conferring on projects; presenting to public stakeholders (task 20374) and collaborating on whole building design (task 19597) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: partners upload drawings to the common data environment, on about 70% of projects; s2 is priced at that share.
s4 saves the second entry of issues from minutes into the issue list.
Conferring, checking and sending the notes keep their full time. Partners' uploads are shown in s6.
unknowns: Share of projects with a common data environment.
research_questions: Do issues close in fewer meetings?

incremental.description: Landscape architect keeps issues in the shared environment current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small clients and partners outside the shared environment, so drawings are still collected from mail (s2 keeps 80) and issues still copied (s4 keeps 85) (9.8); high: about 70% of projects in the shared environment (16.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather site data, visit the site, run slope and drainage analyses, interpret conditions such as site location, drainage and structure location, and write the site analysis for environmental reports or landscaping plans.

steps.what: Landscape architect gathers site data: maps, elevation, soil, groundwater, utilities and structure location
Landscape architect visits the site to observe conditions
Landscape architect runs slope and drainage analyses
Landscape architect interprets the conditions and what they mean for the design
Landscape architect writes the site analysis section of the environmental report or landscaping plan

tasks.design: A GIS project template loads the public map services for the site boundary (topography, elevation, soil, groundwater and cable and pipe records), instead of the architect downloading and aligning each layer. A saved GIS workflow computes slope, flow paths and catchments from the elevation data. The site visit and interpreting conditions stay with the architect. The report template places the maps and tables, and the architect writes the interpretation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layers were downloaded and aligned by hand for each site.
tasks.enabler_now: Public map services and saved GIS workflows.
tasks.still_hard: Sites where public data are outdated or coarse.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing on site where water actually stands after rain.

reach.learn: Whether site data arrive sooner and in one format.

evidence.claim: The national topographic base map is renewed five times a year per region from aerial and panoramic photos and served online.
Design and site analysis: simulation is deterministic; the design stays with the designer.

assumptions: Boundary: analysing site data; conceptual drawings of predicted growth (task 20381) are a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: public map services cover topography, elevation and soil for Dutch sites; utility records still need a request.
The site visit and interpreting keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of site analyses per year.
research_questions: Is site analysis done sooner in the design schedule?

incremental.description: Landscape architect maintains the GIS template and workflows.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual sites with custom data outside the public services, so s1 keeps 70 and the saved workflow needs adapting, so s3 keeps 80 (14.5); high: standard Dutch sites as designed (26.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Draw the site plan, take off quantities, price the cost estimate, write the specifications for land development, and check plan, specifications and estimate together.

steps.what: Landscape architect draws the site plans
Landscape architect takes off quantities from the plan
Landscape architect prices the quantities into cost estimates
Landscape architect writes the specifications
Landscape architect checks plan, specifications and estimate together

tasks.design: Objects in the site plan (paving, planting, earthwork, furniture) carry codes, so quantities are taken off from the model instead of measured by hand. The take-off codes link to a price table, so the estimate is priced with the architect checking unusual items. Specification clauses come from a specification library linked to the same codes, and the architect edits project-specific clauses. Drawing the plan and the final check stay with the architect.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quantities were measured and priced in spreadsheets, and clauses copied from old projects.
tasks.enabler_now: Model-based quantity take-off and coded specification libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Bespoke elements without codes or prices.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which cheap paving will fail on this soil.
tasks.altitude: Less measuring and copying; design stays.

reach.learn: Whether estimates match tender prices more closely.

evidence.claim: Model checking software does rule-based checks and quantity take-off.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing plans, specifications and estimates; collaborating with estimators and coordinating contractor bids (task 20380) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: price table kept by the estimators, covering about 70% of items; s3 is priced at that share.
Drawing and the final check keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of objects with codes in current drawings.
research_questions: Do estimates and specifications need fewer corrections?

incremental.description: Landscape architect codes objects consistently while drawing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: bespoke designs with few coded items, so take-off (s2 keeps 60), pricing (s3 keeps 80) and specifications (s4 keeps 85) stay mostly by hand (11.5); high: standard development with coded items (25.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Survey existing trees, water and terrain, map them into the base drawing, decide how to integrate existing land features into designs, and check the design against protection zones and levels.

steps.what: Landscape architect surveys existing trees, water and terrain on site
Landscape architect maps existing land features into the base drawing
Landscape architect decides which features to keep and how to integrate them into the design
Landscape architect checks the design against root protection zones and existing levels

tasks.design: The surveyor's and arborist's digital surveys are imported as objects with species, size, level and protection zone, instead of the architect redrawing them from paper. The site survey and deciding what to keep stay with the architect. A rule check flags design objects inside root protection zones or that change levels near kept features, and the architect resolves each flag.
tasks.previous_blocker: Surveys arrived on paper or as flat drawings and were redrawn.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital tree and terrain surveys and rule-based model checks.
tasks.still_hard: Old trees whose roots do not follow standard zones.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which old tree gives the place its character.
tasks.altitude: Less redrawing and checking; design choices stay.

reach.learn: Whether more kept trees survive construction.

evidence.claim: Model checking software runs rule-based checks and clash detection.

assumptions: Boundary: integrating existing features; water-saving planting (task 19598) and rainwater systems (task 19599) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: surveyors and arborists deliver digital surveys with attributes, on about 70% of projects; s2 is priced at that share.
Surveying on site and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of surveys delivered with attributes.
research_questions: Are fewer kept trees damaged during construction?

incremental.description: Landscape architect sets up protection zone rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: surveys mostly delivered on paper, so features are still redrawn and s2 keeps 85 (10.2); high: about 70% digital surveys as assumed (17.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
